sentences.text: The application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, by the accused in Crime No.2588/2023 of the Kottarakkara Police Station, Kollam, registered against him for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Secs.419 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code (in short, 'IPC') and Section 66(D) of the Information Technology Act.

The petitioner was arrested on 24.01.2024.
2.

The crux of the prosecution case is that: the accused had impersonated himself with an intention to cheat the defacto complainant and induced him to like the you tube channels on the assurance that he could earn money.

Initially the accused rewarded the defacto complainant with Rs.300/-
after completing three initial tasks.
After gaining his confidence, the accused insisted the defacto complainant to transfer an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- to the bank account.
Thereafter, the accused did not pay profit to the defacto complainant.
Thus, he has BAIL APPL.
NO. 1590 OF 2024 committed the above offences.

3. Heard; Sri.T.S.Sarath, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Smt.Shinymol V.O., the learned Public Prosecutor and Sri.Sabikh Mohammed, the learned counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent - defacto complainant.
4.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is totally innocent of the accusations leveled against him.
He has been falsely implicated in the crime.
The offences under Sections 419 and 420 will not stand attracted in the crime.
Notwithstanding the contentions raised in the bail application, the subject matter in dispute between the petitioner and the 3 rd respondent has been amicably settled out of court.
The petitioner has paid the entire money to the 3 rd respondent/defacto complainant.
In any given given case, the petitioner has been in judicial custody since BAIL APPL. NO. 1590 OF 2024 24.01.2024, that the investigation in the case is complete and recovery has been effected.
Therefore, the petitioner's further detention is unnecessary.
Hence, the application may be allowed.
5. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
Nonetheless she conceded to the fact that the petitioner has been in judicial custody since 24.01.2024, that the investigation in the case is complete and recovery has been effected.

6. The learned counsel appearing for the 3 rd respondent/defacto complainant submitted that the subject matter in dispute between the petitioner and the 3rd respondent has been amicably settled and the petitioner has returned the entire amount to the 3 rd respondent.
The said submission is recorded.

7. On a consideration of the facts, the rival BAIL APPL. NO. 1590 OF 2024 submissions made across the Bar and the materials placed on record, especially taking into account the fact that the petitioner Mujeeb N vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49511409/
2 has been in judicial custody since 24.01.2024, that the investigation in the case is practically complete and recovery has been effected and further the dispute between the petitioner and the 3 rd respondent has been settled out of court, I am of the view that the petitioner's further detention is unnecessary.

sentences.text: Hence, I am inclined to allow the bail application.

In the result, the application is allowed, by directing the petitioner to be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction, which shall be subject to the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on every Saturday between 9 BAIL APPL. NO. 1590 OF 2024 a.m. and 11 a.m for a period of one month or till the final report is laid, whichever is earlier.

If he has no passport, he shall file an affidavit to the effect before the court below on the date of execution of the bond;
(v) The petitioner shall furnish his present address and permanent address, and his mobile phone number to the court below and the Investigating Officer;

(vi) In case of violation of any of the conditions mentioned above, the jurisdictional court shall be BAIL APPL. NO. 1590 OF 2024 empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any filed, and pass orders on the same, in accordance with law.
(vii) Applications for deletion/modification of the bail conditions shall be moved and entertained by the court below.

(viii) Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the Investigating Officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Anr.
[2020 (1) KHC 663].
